A matrix stores numbers in rows and columns, while a vector records the coordinates of one object. Students compare matrix and vector calculations to check their answers.
The determinant of a square matrix helps determine whether a system has a unique solution. Exchanging two rows changes the sign of the determinant.
Cramer method solves a small system of linear equations by replacing one column at a time. Each unknown is found as a ratio of two determinants.
A basis provides a way to describe a vector using a fixed set of independent vectors. New coordinates describe the same vector in a different basis.
An ellipse becomes easier to describe after a rotation of the coordinate axes and a shift of the origin. Its two semiaxes determine the size of the curve.
A hyperbola has two separate branches and two asymptotes that describe their directions. Students draw the curve after completing squares in its equation.
A parabola has a vertex and an axis that indicates the direction in which it opens. Completing a square helps locate the vertex in the original coordinates.
Cosine similarity compares the directions of two vectors rather than their absolute lengths. A document and a search query can be compared using their vector representations.
TF IDF gives each word a weight based on its frequency in a document and its rarity across the collection. A rare word can help distinguish documents about different topics.
A search engine converts a query into a vector and ranks documents by their similarity to that query. Documents with the same score are ordered by their original indices.
Tokenization separates an English sentence into individual words and removes punctuation from the resulting tokens. Different forms of a word remain separate entries in this simple vocabulary.
A library stores books about mathematics, history, music, and science in several rooms. Readers use a catalog to find a book that matches their interests.
A neural network uses numerical weights to combine information from many input features. During training the network adjusts these weights using examples with known answers.
A neural network can classify a small image after its pixels have been arranged into a vector. The quality of its predictions depends on both the data and the model.
A computer program checks mathematical formulas using small examples with known results. Tests help students find mistakes before they run calculations on a larger dataset.
A student writes Python functions to count words in a collection of short documents. The program prints a frequency table and saves the results for comparison.
A cat sleeps near the sunny window while a dog waits quietly beside the door. Later the cat follows a moving shadow across the kitchen floor.
A young cat watches small birds from a garden fence every morning. The birds collect seeds under a tree and fly away when the cat approaches.
A dog runs through the park while its owner walks along a narrow path. After a long game the dog rests near a bench in the shade.
A bird builds a nest in a tall tree beside the river. In the evening several birds return to the same tree and sing above the water.
A train leaves the city station early in the morning and stops at several small towns. Passengers read books or watch the fields through the windows.
Heavy rain falls on the garden while dark clouds move slowly across the sky. After the rain stops sunlight appears and the wet leaves become bright.
A musician plays a quiet melody on the piano while other students listen in the classroom. The music becomes louder when the whole group begins to sing.
A cook prepares fresh vegetables and rice for a simple evening meal. Everyone gathers around the kitchen table and discusses the events of the day.
